note.text: An occupation is a kind of work. A duty is a task involved in it; a skill is an ability used to perform tasks; a qualification records a recognised educational or training achievement. These ideas are connected but not identical. Training routes and entry rules vary and may change. This lesson teaches how to ask about them, not current professional eligibility. Check exact requirements with the appropriate institution before making a real application.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original dialogue: Ayuk asks what a laboratory worker does. Bih explains that duties may involve careful record-keeping and following supervised procedures. Ayuk asks which training route the relevant institution recognises. Bih says they should check the institution's current information rather than assume that liking science alone qualifies someone to practise.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Describe work with precise verbs, then ask how a skill relates to a duty. Distinguish general interest from a formal requirement. In a written comparison, avoid promising employment, a salary or admission. Label fictional examples clearly.
